description.narrative:
Svenska ambassaden har fått en förfrågan från The Carter Center och Liberia Election Observation Network (LEON) att finansiera projektet "Strengthening citizen voices to advance electoral reform and democratic governance" med 31 300 000 kronor under perioden 2021-2024.
Det övergripande målet för denna insats är att LEON år 2024 ska ha ökad kapacitet att på egen hand bidra till att stärka demokratiska val och informerade medborgare genom icke-partisk och evidensbaserad valobervation och granskning av demokratiska processer.
Denna projekperiod kommer att fokusera på följande områden:
1) Påverkansarbete inom konstitutionella reformer samt valreformer
2) Följa och rapportera arbetet inom den lagstiftande församlingen i syfte att öka transparens
3) Ansvarsskyldighet och medborgarengagemang
4) Genomföra diskussionsgrupper för att säkerställa medborgarnas bidrag till policy och reformer
5) Genomföra nationella enkätundersökningar som genererar policypåverkan
6) Bidra till diskussioner på länsnivå för att åtgärda bristen på tillgång till information utanför Monrovia
7) Genomföra valobservation i fyllnadsval och i det nationella valet 2023

The Carter Center and Liberia Election Observation Network (LEON) have applied to the Swedish Embassy for funding of 31 300 000 SEK to carry out the project "Strengthening citizen voices to advance electoral reform and democratic governance" during the period 2021-2024.
The overall goal of this intervention is that by 2024, LEON will have increased capacity to operate independently and will have contributed to the strengthening of democratic elections, governance, and an informed citizenry through credible non-partisan and evidence-based citizen observation around elections and democratic processes.
This project phase will focus on the following main areas of activity:
1. advocacy on electoral and constitutional reforms
2. monitoring the legislative branch to improve transparency
3. accountability, and citizen engagement
4. conducting discussion groups to ensure citizen input on legislative and government programs
5. conducting national surveys that generate results that can guide policy
6. facilitation of county-level discussions on key topics to address information gaps outside of Monrovia
7. observation of legislative by-elections and the 2023 national elections

The overall goal of this intervention is that by 2024, LEON will have increased capacity to operate independently and will have contributed to the strengthening of democratic elections, governance, and an informed citizenry through credible non-partisan and evidence-based citizen observation around elections and democratic processes. The intervention has two objectives: Objective 1: LEON has increased organizational capacity to manage projects and enhance their long-term sustainability. Objective 2: LEON is a credible and non-partisan organization that contributes to strengthening inclusive and participatory democratic processes and institutions in Liberia through programming in advocacy, election observation, surveys, and legislative monitoring.

description.narrative:
In the most recent annual report, covering the period June 2023 until July 2024, the below results were achieved. Since this report, Sida made the decision to extend the agreement with the Carter Center for a phaseout period.
Examples of achievements during June 2023 July 2024:
1.Objective One organizational capacity:
-LEON demonstrated its operational planning abilities during the successful implementation of its election observation mission (EOM) during the 2023 general elections. More than 2,000 long and shortterm observers (LTO/STOs) and core team members were recruited, trained, deployed, managed, and paid during the legislative and both rounds of presidential elections.
-LEON continued to strengthen its organizational capacity in several areas. As shown by the capacity assessment, LEON has gradually improved in all seven areas measured (1: Organizational governance, leadership and strategic management, 2: Programming, 3: Monitoring and evaluation, 4: Communications, media and public information, 5: Financial management and procurement, 6: Administrative management, 7: Human resources management). In particular, LEON has strengthened its administrative management.
-LEON also achieved organizational restructuring by developing and implementing a proposal to refocus activities and reduce operations to encourage post-election sustainability.
-LEONs administrative and financial capacity was further demonstrated in the independent audit, which issued an unqualified opinion and indicated that its review of LEONs financial statements provided a fair representation of its position and performance during the second year (202223). LEON also successfully opened its own local bank account in September 2023 as a step towards independently managing its own finances apart from Liberia Crusaders for Peaces banking control.
2.Objective Two programming in advocacy, election observation, surveys, legislative monitoring:
-LEON researched and published its first policy brief by June 2024, which issued calls for action on five legal framework topics. LEON will use this policy brief as a springboard for stimulating national discussion among civil society, legislators, executive office holders, electoral officials, and other stakeholders to inspire citizen engagement strategies and establish policy dialogue platforms with the aim of setting advocacy agendas.
-LEON observed candidate nomination, campaigning and rallies, civic and voter education, legislative and two rounds of presidential elections, electoral dispute resolution, court-ordered reruns and recounts, and subsequent legislative by elections. LEON applied an advanced sample-based observation (SBO) methodology for the first-time in Liberia, during both rounds of the presidential election. The results projections were consistent with the official results of the National Elections Commission (NEC), which contributed to public confidence in the electoral process.
-LEON also continued to conduct surveys to provide the public with reliable information of national interest. LEON conducted both a preelection survey and a post-election survey. Both surveys focused on the public perception, and showed that people were dissatisfied with the previous administration, that they wanted to see some change and that they expect the new administration to be more responsive to good governance and provide more basic services.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
